source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Heater and Air Conditioning, p.1A-19

procedures.title: Gauge set: description
notes: The only time both manifold valves are opened together is to bypass refrigerant vapor from the high side to the low side, or to evacuate both sides.
The charging station supplies two flexible lines to connect the gauge set to the system.

procedures.title: Vacuum pump: operation and maintenance
steps: Take the dust cap off the pump discharge outlet before running the pump.
Keep all openings capped when idle so moisture is not drawn into the system.
Change the oil every 250 hours of normal use: unscrew the hex nut on the back of the pump, tilt the pump back and drain the oil.
Refill with 8 ounces of vacuum pump oil (Frigidaire 150 or equivalent); to flush the pump use the same clean oil, never solvent.
After extreme or long exposure to cold, leave the pump indoors until the oil is near room temperature, or the fuse will blow.
If the fuse blows, replace it only with a 5 ampere time delay fuse; a substitute will damage the starting windings.
When evacuating a burnt-out system, fit a filter on the intake fitting to keep sludge out of the pump.
Do not use the vacuum pump as an air compressor.
notes: Used to remove air and moisture from the system; part of the J-8393 charging station (see figure 26 in the manual).
The fuse in the common line protects the motor windings and blows under excessive load.

procedures.title: Refrigerant leak testing
notes: Leak test whenever a leak is suspected or after work that disturbs lines or connections; how much testing depends on the complaint and the work done. When in doubt, test.

Leak-detecting dye in the system is not recommended: refrigerant can leak with no oil leak (dye misses it, a torch detector does not); additives other than inhibitors can upset system stability; insoluble dyes can curdle and block the expansion valve inlet screen.
Leak Detector J-6084 (see figure 27 in the manual) is a propane torch; R-12 drawn into its sampling tube changes the flame color in proportion to the leak size.
